paper.title: MetaClaw: Just Talk -- An Agent That Meta-Learns and Evolves in the Wild
paper.central_claim: MetaClaw: continual meta-learning that jointly maintains a base LLM policy and an evolving skill library; gradient-free skill evolution from failures takes effect immediately, while opportunistic LoRA RL (during user-idle windows) with skill-generation versioning separates support and query data; improves accuracy on MetaClaw-Bench (Kimi-K2.5 21.4%->40.6%) and robustness on AutoResearchClaw.

provenance.notes: Opus aggregate seat via the configured claude-kimi type fable; no route probing. actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref are null because the subagent runtime exposes no verifiable provider receipt to this worker.

claims.text: Skill-driven fast adaptation alone improves accuracy by up to 32% relative.
claims.setting: MetaClaw-Bench Part I (346 Q, 30 days) and II (588 Q, 14 days); GPT-5.2, Kimi-K2.5
claims.baseline_control: Same model and prompts without skills
claims.selection_vs_test: Online stream; skills learned from earlier days applied to later days; no separate held-out stream
claims.result_denominator: Accuracy: GPT 41.1->44.0, 44.9->49.1; Kimi 21.4->28.3, 21.1->26.9; completion unchanged on Part I
claims.allowed_conclusion: On this authored simulation, skills-on beats skills-off by roughly 3-7 accuracy points in single runs; Part I completion is not improved.

claims.result_denominator: Part I acc 40.6, compl 16.5; Part II acc 39.6, compl 51.9; multi-choice declines
claims.allowed_conclusion: Full > skills-only > baseline for one model/run on this stream; RL's own contribution vs in-stream fine-tuning generally, and skills/weights mutual reinforcement, are not isolated.

claims.text: Skill-generation versioning prevents stale-reward contamination and is essential; OMLS removes downtime.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Untested design claims; text on buffer contents is inconsistent.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On the authors' simulated 30/14-day CLI stream, failure-distilled prompt skills accumulated over the stream raise later-day accuracy by about 3-7 points over a no-skill run (single runs); a 5-day LoRA RL run on one model adds further gains whose attribution is not isolated.
assessment.unresolved: Versioning/OMLS/retrieval necessity; weights-only control; real-user transfer; buffer semantics; cost; variance; nearest neighbours uncompared.
assessment.evidence_note: Opus: 'retained' as in both seats. Skills distilled on earlier days are reused on later days of the same stream (e.g., a Day 2 skill used on Day 19), and the same-backbone skills-on/off toggle isolates the skill arm. This is narrow: online stream, no held-out stream, single runs.

G.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Static skill libraries and stale RL rewards after skill changes are concrete gaps, but 'no existing system unifies' is untested, and co-evolution neighbours (EvolveR, SkillRL-type) are not compared.

M.reason: Opus sides with son55. The two-timescale design and the support/query rationale are coherent and responsive. The 'meta-learning' claim, that θ is trained to become better at adapting, is not carried by any objective: the evolver is a fixed prompt, and Eq. 4 is ordinary RL on skill-conditioned rollouts. 'Mutually reinforcing' is asserted only (son55:E027). The buffer rationale is internally inconsistent (son55:E013, son55:E014, opus:O02). sol's 3 credits interface clarity, which is X's question.

X.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Algorithm 1, versioning, OMLS signals, the evolver prompt and the injection format are given. k, the embedder, the failure threshold, the evolver model and the PRM are unspecified. The library is add-only with no gate or rollback. Buffer semantics conflict across §3.3/§3.4/Alg. 1.

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Deterministic checkers and a stated multi-choice scoring rule exist, but the benchmark is self-authored with rule-revealing feedback, the RL reward is a learned PRM, and the AutoResearchClaw composite is an author-defined process metric. Added: the text says skills-only leaves Part I completion 'unchanged for both models', while Table 1 has GPT-5.2 14.7→17.1 (opus:O01). Within the cap.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked. Skills-on/off with identical prompts and tools isolates the skill arm. There is no weights-only arm, no versioning/OMLS/retrieval ablation and no raw-trajectory memory baseline, and Full is one run on one model, so the coupling claim is not isolated.

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked. The learning and reporting streams coincide with no declared split, and the per-round feedback states the hidden rules. The second domain reuses one topic across runs. This is an in-claim online setting (cf. r11a TTE = 1), so not 0.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1 (A2 ladder): 346/588-question denominators and negative cells (Kimi Part I completion 2.0→2.0; multi-choice decline under Full) are reported, but there are no seeds, variance or tests, and Full is a single run.

E.cost.reason: Opus sides with son55. The only quantitative resource disclosure is the '5-day training run' (sol:E07). There are no GPU hours, API/PRM/evolver calls, prompt-token overhead or interruption measurements, and zero downtime is architectural. A wall-clock disclosure without totals rates 1 under run precedent (r05a 'Agents of Change': 60 h wall-clock = 1). not_reported would require no cost-relevant figure at all.
